feedback.description: this memory records a correction somebody gave, and who gave it

memory.description: one thing a person said about how they want something built or handled, kept in their own words. The words themselves are the entity's doc.body, verbatim; these columns record where they belong and what is needed to read them. The byline is the entity's created{at, by}

space.description: whose space they were said in — every member of that space can read them, and they are deleted with it

about.description: the app they were said about, by slug, when they were about one

context.description: the line or two needed to understand the words — what was being talked about, never a restatement of what was said

memory_save.title: Save a memory
memory_save.description: Save what somebody said, in their own words. The memory is the sentence itself, never your summary of it, which can only hold less, plus a line or two of context somebody will need to read it weeks later. scope names the project it belongs to; leave it out for a principle that applies everywhere. feedback names who gave the correction, when the words are one. Pass id to patch an existing memory instead of creating one: anything left out is unchanged, and replacing the words requires was, the token memory_recall returns beside them, so a memory another writer changed since you read it is refused whole rather than overwritten.

said.description: the words the person used, as they used them

title.description: the index line a recall shows first

context.description: what was being discussed, in two lines; never a restatement of what was said

scope.description: the project the memory belongs to; leave it out for one that applies everywhere

feedback.description: who gave the correction these words are: a person, or empty when nobody knows. Either way the memory is marked as feedback

about.description: the app the words were said about, by slug

id.description: an existing memory to patch instead of creating one

was.description: the token memory_recall returned beside the words you are replacing

memory_recall.title: Recall memories
memory_recall.description: Return the memories closest to what you are doing. said is matched against their text as a phrase, so pass the words you expect the memory to contain rather than a sentence of your own. near names an entity and ranks by meaning instead, where this server keeps vectors; that is the ranking that answers a sentence. With neither, the newest are returned. Each memory is returned whole, since half of what somebody said is worse than none of it, and carries the $was token memory_save requires before replacing it.

said.description: the words you expect the memory to contain, matched as a phrase

near.description: an entity to rank by meaning against, where this server keeps vectors

scope.description: only memories filed under this project

feedback.description: only memories recording a correction somebody gave
